summary: A grid of 7 days by 24 hours where darker cells mean busier hours, so people can see when the agent and the team do their work. Hovering a cell gives the exact count for that day and hour. A switch flips between series, such as the agent's runs and the team's edits, and the cells refill in a wave.
use: When you want to show when an agent runs, for example overnight when a queue is processed.
When comparing the agent's working hours with the team's.
When planning when to schedule jobs or reviews around busy periods.
features: Takes 168 values from 0 to 1 per series, one per hour starting Monday 12am, and shades each cell by its value.
Hovering a cell shows a tooltip like "Monday 9am: 40 runs", using the series' `max` and `unit`.
With two or more entries in `series`, a switch picks which one shows.
The line under the title shows the series' `note`, or `period` when it has none.
Cells fill in as a wave from the top left when the card appears and when the series changes.
Day labels down the side, hour labels along the bottom and a Less to More legend.

In a narrow card (400px or less, as on a phone) the grid shows half the day at a time in bigger cells and scrolls sideways by touch or trackpad, starting at the latest hours. The day labels stay put, the side with more to see fades out, and the hour labels come every three hours.
a11y: The grid has role="img" with an aria-label made of the title and the current note or period.
The day labels, hour labels and legend are aria-hidden.
The series switch is a role="group" labelled "Who", with aria-pressed on the active option.
The wave delay between cells is removed when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.q: What shape does the data need to be?
faq.a: Each series needs exactly 168 numbers between 0 and 1, one per hour, Monday 12am first and Sunday 11pm last. Scale your counts down first; the tooltips multiply by `max` to show real counts again.

faq.q: How do the tooltip counts work?
faq.a: A cell's value times the series' `max`, rounded, followed by its `unit`. So 0.5 with `max: 40` and `unit: 'runs'` reads "20 runs".

faq.q: Can I show just one series without the switch?
faq.a: Yes. Pass a single entry in `series`. The switch only appears when there are two or more.
